title: Lists
summary: Keep many values in order and loop over them with for.

blocks.text: A list holds several values in order, between square brackets:

code: print(kinds[-1])      # Skeleton: -1 is the last one

blocks.text: Lists can grow and shrink: kinds.append("Troll") adds to the end, kinds.pop() removes the last item.

blocks.tip: Counting from 0 is normal in almost every programming language. The first item is [0], the second is [1].

blocks.text: A 'for' loop runs its body once for every item in a list, putting the item in a variable each time:
enemies() gives a list of every enemy the golem can see, nearest first. range(n) gives the numbers 0 to n-1, handy for repeating something an exact number of times:
A very common pattern: loop over a list and return the first item that matches. As soon as return runs, the loop and the function end.

blocks.text: path_to(target) also returns a list: every [x, y] step to a target. len(path_to(stairs())) tells you how far the stairs really are, walls included.

challenge.brief: Bats swarm the roost around two chests. Write adjacent_enemy(): loop over enemies() with for and return the first one next to you. Open both chests, then take the stairs.
